entries.finding: Kokori et al. 2023 (2023ApJS..265....4K), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname KOKORI_ET_AL__2023): P 2.21674331 d; Stassun et al. 2017 (2017AJ....153..136S), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname STASSUN_ET_AL__2017): a/R* 4.61; Stassun et al. 2017 (2017AJ....153..136S), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname STASSUN_ET_AL__2017): inclination 86.8 degrees; Stassun et al. 2017 (2017AJ....153..136S), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname STASSUN_ET_AL__2017): e 0; Kokori et al. 2023 (2023ApJS..265....4K), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname KOKORI_ET_AL__2023): transit mid-time 2458789.06301 BJD, taken as BJD_TDB; with its period, the row that predicts 2026-01-01 best (1 sigma 1 min); Display convention: transit photometry does not measure the orbit's position angle on the sky, so the ascending node is set at position angle 0 (celestial north)..

entries.subject: Published TESS phase curve as a map of longitude (Wong et al. 2020)
entries.finding: Read on 2026-10-08. Wong et al. (2020, arXiv:2003.06407) fit TESS sectors 3 and 4 (A_atm 70 +15/-16 ppm, D_d 113 +39/-31 ppm, D_n -28 +38/-31 ppm) and print no temperature for this planet: it has no Spitzer eclipse and is absent from the paper's temperature table.
entries.revisitWhen: A paper prints day-side and night-side brightness temperatures from a sinusoid fit of one band.
